title: Variant Performance Dashboard
description: Five kernel implementations compared across kernel time, total time, code size, and memory, with a drag-to-reorder prediction overlay scored against the measured ranking for whichever metric is active.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Benchmarking
Performance Engineering

educational.topic: Multi-metric comparison and the metric-dependence of a ranking
learningObjectives: Assess a predicted ranking against a measured ranking
Critique which metric answers the shipping decision
Explain why fixed overhead caps an end-to-end speedup
prerequisites: Familiarity with the five implementation strategies
Flash and RAM budgets on an embedded part

controls.label: Metric
controls.purpose: Re-render the bars and the measured ranking in the chosen metric

controls.label: Overlay my ranking prediction
controls.purpose: Show the prediction row and its score

controls.label: Bar
controls.purpose: Exact value and rank on the active metric

simulationModel.modelType: Fixed multi-metric measurement table with a learner-supplied ranking scored against it
equations: measured order = variants sorted ascending, since every metric is lower-is-better
score = count of positions where predicted index equals measured index
assumptions: All four metrics are lower-is-better, stated in the controls bar
Values are illustrative and internally consistent
Ties are possible and are shown rather than broken
limitations: Kernel time and total time happen to produce the same ranking in this data set
No variance or repeated runs; each value is a single point
Metrics are not combined into a weighted score, deliberately

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Commit to a prediction first, then re-score the same prediction under every metric
keyQuestions: Which metric were you ranking by when you made your prediction?
Why does the overhead grow relative to the kernel as the kernel gets faster?
commonMisconceptions: That there is one performance ranking
That kernel speedup and end-to-end speedup are the same number
That a tie is a missing measurement rather than a real result
assessmentOpportunities: Choose a variant to ship under two different flash budgets and justify each
List three questions to ask someone who reports a 30x speedup
